prop:p-bandwidth-bound:
Proposition Polynomial computation as sub-horizon bandwidth. A decision problem encoded by a link L = \hat{\beta} with c = 3N crossings belongs to \mathrm{P} if and only if its Skein polynomial P_L(q) can be evaluated (its degree-0 answer extracted) within

  t(c) \leq \mathfrak{B}(q)^{-1} \mathrm{poly}(c)

Planck steps, where \mathfrak{B}(q) = q\eta_q / (q-1)^2 is the information bandwidth per Planck time.
prf:p-bandwidth-bound:
Proof Proof of p bandwidth bound. Sketch. For the forward direction, one uses the standard simulation. If a polynomial-time Turing machine decides the problem, one encodes it as a braid with c = O(\mathrm{poly}(N)) crossings. The transfer matrix product (transfer matrix) computes P_L(q) using O(c) matrix multiplications. Each multiplication costs O(1) Planck steps.

For the converse, one observes that extracting P_L(q_0) requires resolving the value of a degree \leq c^2 - 1 polynomial at a specific point. Suppose the factored form P_L(q) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i(q) has O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) factors. Then one computes each factor in O(1) steps from the local transfer matrix, making the total cost polynomial. If the factored form requires \omega(\mathrm{poly}(c)) factors, the Skein polynomial fails to compress. The information content of the computation exceeds the polynomial bandwidth budget.
rem:p-bandwidth-interpretation:
Remark P-class as a sub-horizon information funnel. The class \mathrm{P} consists of computations whose resolution trees exhibit sufficient destructive interference. Cancellation among the 3^c Skein histories allows the Markov trace to compress the tree to O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) surviving terms. In each Planck step, the q-connection \nabla_q processes n_R(q) = 1/\hbar_q iterations. Each iteration generates \eta_q q-bits of entropy. After t Planck steps, the total information budget is:

  I(t) = t \mathfrak{B}(q) = t \frac{q\eta_q}{(q-1)^2} \quad q\text{-bits.}

A \mathrm{P}-class computation succeeds when I(\mathrm{poly}(c)) suffices to determine P_L(q_0). Although the full resolution tree carries c \log_2 3 q-bits of raw information, destructive interference limits the effective content to O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) q-bits, fitting within the polynomial budget.

Three regimes.

Regime Condition Interpretation
Sub-horizon (P) Effective tree \leq \mathrm{poly}(c) Interference collapses tree; no computational horizon
Critical Effective tree = c^{O(\log c)} Quasi-polynomial; horizon marginally transparent
Super-horizon (NP-hard) Effective tree = 2^{\Omega(c)} Horizon opaque; bandwidth saturated exponentially

In the sub-horizon regime, the Markov trace funnels the 3^c paths through the degree-0 bottleneck in polynomial time. The computation avoids any computational horizon; the answer remains accessible from a polynomial-depth subtree.

In the super-horizon regime, the resolution tree retains irreducible exponential weight. The uncancelled paths carry independent information requiring full aggregation. Because the bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q) per Planck step is finite, this demands exponentially many steps. A computational horizon strictly separates the answer from the observer.
def:polynomial-observable-subcategory:
Definition Polynomial observable subcategory of a resolution tree. Let \beta be a braid on n strands with c crossings, let L = \hat{\beta} be its closure, let \mathcal{R}(L) be the Skein resolution tree (Skein Turing machine), and fix a polynomial bound p(c) = c^d. For x \in \mathcal{R}(L), let \Gamma_{\mathrm{poly}}(x, A_0) be the set of degree-0 sections at x that the Markov trace computes in at most p(c) Planck steps. The polynomial observable subcategory of the resolution tree is the full sub-poset

  \mathcal{R}^{\circ}(L, q)
  = 
  \bigl\{
    x \in \mathcal{R}(L)
     : 
    \Gamma_{\mathrm{poly}}\!(x, A_0) \neq 0
  \bigr\}.
rem:polynomial-observable-subcategory-re: Remark The polynomial observable subcategory as a computational analogue. The Markov trace defining \Gamma_{\mathrm{poly}} restricts to \mathcal{R}_{p(c)}.
def:computational-boundary:
Definition Computational boundary of a resolution tree. Let \mathcal{R}^{\circ}(L, q) be the polynomial observable subcategory of the resolution tree. The computational boundary is the frontier

  \mathcal{H}_c(L, q) = \overline{\mathcal{R}^{\circ}} \setminus \mathcal{R}^{\circ}.
rem:computational-boundary-remark:
Remark The computational boundary as a vanishing locus. Equivalently, the computational boundary is the vanishing locus of the computational horizon ideal:

  \mathcal{H}_c(L, q) = V\!\bigl(\mathfrak{h}_c\bigr), \qquad
  \mathfrak{h}_c = \bigl\{ s \in \Gamma\bigl(\mathcal{R}, A_0^{\mathrm{comp}}\bigr) : s\big|_{\mathcal{H}_c} = 0 \bigr\}.

This frontier is the locus in the resolution tree where every polynomial-time degree-0 section vanishes. It structurally mirrors the jet horizon \mathcal{H} = V(\mathfrak{h}), substituting the resolution tower for the brane tower and the Iwahori--Hecke algebra for the Frobenius algebra.
conj:p-vs-np-boundary:
Conjecture \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} as jet horizon opacity. Let L = \hat{\beta} be the closure of a braid \beta encoding a decision problem. Let \mathcal{H}_c(L, q) denote its computational boundary.

  \mathrm{P} = \mathrm{NP} \Longleftrightarrow \mathcal{H}_c(L, q) = \varnothing \text{ for every NP link } L

Consequently, \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} if and only if there exists an NP-complete link L carrying a non-empty computational horizon:

  \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} \Longleftrightarrow \exists L \text{ (NP-complete)} \text{ with } \mathcal{H}_c(L, q) \neq \varnothing.

The formal conjecture. For the QOU at a non-torsion aether parameter q_0 \in \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}(\mathbb{R}), there exists a family of braids \{L_N = \hat{\beta}_N\}_{N \geq 1} with c_N = 3N crossings encoding an NP-complete problem such that:

  \mathcal{H}_c(L_N, q_0) \neq \varnothing \qquad \text{for all } N \geq N_0.

This non-empty boundary establishes a genuine event horizon within the resolution tree, implying \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} over \mathbb{R} at q = q_0.

rem:p-vs-np-boundary-interpretation:
Remark Geometric meaning of the boundary dichotomy and the three equivalent criteria. Geometric meaning of each case.

  • \mathcal{H}_c = \varnothing (P = NP): The polynomial observable subcategory \mathcal{R}^{\circ} is closed. Every degree-0 section existing in \mathcal{R} already extends to polynomial depth. The computational horizon ideal vanishes: \mathfrak{h}_c = (0). No information barrier separates the polynomial slice from the full tree. The resolution tree exhibits no genuine boundary; it harbors a removable singularity.
  • \mathcal{H}_c \neq \varnothing (P \neq NP): The polynomial observable subcategory \mathcal{R}^{\circ} is not closed. A non-trivial computational boundary manifests as a codimension-1 locus where degree-0 sections vanish. The horizon ideal \mathfrak{h}_c \neq (0) captures polynomial-time algorithms that reach the boundary and return 0. The resolution tree exhibits a genuine event horizon, forming an essential singularity.

Parallel with the jet horizon and NS obstruction. See Table 1.

The three equivalent criteria for \mathcal{H}_c \neq \varnothing.

  1. Ideal-theoretic. The horizon ideal is non-trivial: \mathfrak{h}_c \neq (0). Polynomial-time algorithms evaluate to 0 on the boundary.
  2. Cohomological. The Skein resolution obstruction class does not vanish: \kappa_c^{\mathrm{comp}}(L, q) \neq 0. This class obstructs the lift from polynomial depth to full resolution.
  3. Information-theoretic. The effective tree size, after interference, strictly exceeds the polynomial bandwidth budget: I(\mathrm{poly}(c)) < c \cdot \log 3 q-bits.

Connection to quantum computation. The descent involution \hat{\tau} acts directly on the boundary. At a root of unity q_k:

  \mathcal{H}_c(L, q_k) = \mathcal{H}_c^{\mathrm{desc}} \cup \mathcal{H}_c^{\mathrm{trans}}.

The descended boundary \mathcal{H}_c^{\mathrm{desc}} constitutes the classical horizon, remaining opaque at real q. The transient boundary \mathcal{H}_c^{\mathrm{trans}} supplies the quantum correction. For BQP problems, exact cancellation occurs: \mathcal{H}_c^{\mathrm{trans}} = -\mathcal{H}_c^{\mathrm{desc}}. This yields \mathcal{H}_c = \varnothing at the root of unity. The boundary completely dissolves under quantum interference.

rem:p-vs-np-event-horizon:
Remark P versus NP through the event horizon: information loss and computational irreversibility. One formally establishes a structural identity between computational complexity and jet horizon information loss. Reformulating \mathrm{P} vs \mathrm{NP} as the boundary condition \mathcal{H}_c \stackrel{?}{=} \varnothing equates the computational boundary with a jet horizon. The identical horizon geometry \mathcal{H} = V(\mathfrak{h}) that blocks degree-0 photon data between aeons simultaneously blocks the degree-0 answer of an NP-complete problem.

The dictionary. The physical QOU observer corresponds to an element of the observable subcategory \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)). Here, the degree-0 algebra A_0 is non-trivial and the Frobenius pairing is non-degenerate. The complement (A_0 = 0) defines the jet horizon. The computational analog maps directly onto this geometry. See Table 1.

The observer in \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} versus the observer in \mathcal{R}^{\circ}. In the physical QOU, observation requires \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0) \neq 0. The observer performs degree-0 measurements because the Frobenius pairing is non-degenerate on A_0. At the jet horizon, A_0 = 0. The observer loses all degree-0 capability. It still detects degree \geq 1 data, capturing thermal winding and curvature as Hawking radiation, but it cannot identify individual particles.

In the computational setting, the observer is a polynomial-time algorithm inhabiting \mathcal{R}^{\circ}. It accesses degree-0 sections, evaluating P_L(q), strictly from nodes within \mathcal{R}^{\circ}. At the computational boundary \mathcal{H}_c, the algorithm loses degree-0 capability. It retains the ability to verify witnesses via degree-1 linear transport and detect structural correlations via degree-2 curvature data, but it cannot extract the answer. A physics-side precedent links horizons and computational hardness directly: Harlow and Hayden argue that the quantum computation needed to decode the relevant degrees of freedom from Hawking radiation takes time exponential in the entropy of the black hole, and relate the decoding task to error correction and to zero-knowledge proofs [arxiv-1301.4504v4, §3, §4.4].

Information flow across the boundary. The jet horizon leakage table applies directly to computation. See Table 2.

The degree-1 leakage embodies NP verification. Traversing a resolution path in O(c) Planck steps constitutes linear transport. It represents the first jet beyond the constant term. This checks consistency but reveals nothing concerning the global sum P_L(q_0). The degree-2 leakage embodies heuristic computation. Pairwise correlations between resolution paths reveal structural properties like clause-variable correlations. Heuristic algorithms exploit this curvature leakage without worst-case guarantees.

The Planck step as the tick of a Turing machine. Each application of the q-connection \nabla_q constitutes one Planck step. In the computational setting, this mirrors one discrete clock tick of a Turing machine. The Planck time t_P(q) = q/(q-1) sets the fundamental clock rate. The operational entropy \eta_q sets the information generated per tick.

A polynomial-time computation generates I = \mathrm{poly}(c) \cdot \eta_q / \hbar_q q-bits. For P-class problems, this suffices. Destructive interference collapses the effective resolution tree to polynomial size. For NP-complete problems, the effective tree retains exponential size. The computation generates polynomial q-bits but demands exponential q-bits of aggregated information. The bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q) cannot bridge this deficit in polynomial time.

Boundary condition versus resource bound. Standard complexity theory evaluates \mathrm{P} vs \mathrm{NP} as a resource bound. The QOU translates this to a geometric statement: the interior \mathcal{R}^{\circ} is either closed (P = NP) or carries a non-trivial frontier \mathcal{H}_c (P \neq NP).

This matches the physical jet horizon. If \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} is closed, no jet horizons exist. The universe operates as a single transparent aeon without information loss. If \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} is not closed, genuine frontiers exist. The physical QOU structurally possesses jet horizons. The conjecture asserts the computational QOU similarly possesses horizons, with \mathcal{H}_c \neq \varnothing for NP-complete braids.

The arrow of computational time. The Big Bang state initiates with A_0|_{\mathcal{S}_0} = 0. The universe begins outside \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}, behind its own jet horizon. As Planck steps accumulate, the jet tower builds degree-0 sections, moving the universe into \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}.

Computation mirrors this geometric arrow. A Turing machine begins with degree \geq 1 input data. It terminates with degree-0 output data. The computation traverses from \mathcal{R} \setminus \mathcal{R}^{\circ} into \mathcal{R}^{\circ}. For P-class problems, \mathcal{H}_c = \varnothing. The algorithm starts in \mathcal{R}^{\circ} and never leaves. For NP-complete problems, \mathcal{H}_c \neq \varnothing. The algorithm must forcefully cross the boundary, paying the exponential depth of the resolution tree as the crossing cost. The \mathrm{P} vs \mathrm{NP} question becomes geometric: whether the computational observable subcategory covers the full resolution tree.

conj:qou-p-neq-np:
Conjecture \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} at non-torsion q \in \mathbb{G}_m. Conjecture (\mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} in the QOU). Given a QOU with physical non-torsion aether parameter q_0 \in \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}(\mathbb{R}), \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} holds in that QOU. This is a conditional statement: the QOU axioms are its hypothesis — it is not a claim about \mathrm{P} versus \mathrm{NP} in the abstract, and no result here would prove the unconditional Clay problem. Equivalently, the resolution-tree evaluation of the universal obstruction class \chi(A) is non-vanishing:

  \mathrm{res}_{\mathcal{R}}\!\bigl(\chi(A)\bigr)  \neq  0 \qquad\text{at } q = q_0.

The conditioning is explicit: the QOU-scoped separation is derived from the QOU faithfulness hypothesis, and a bare \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} is never concluded.

Established complexity landscape (chippable kernel). The concrete computational object attached to a link L = \hat{\beta} is its Jones invariant J_L(q) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta)), and its complexity is a theorem, stratified by the arithmetic of q:

  • Exact evaluation is \#\mathrm{P}-hard at all but finitely many q (Jaeger--Vertigan--Welsh). The only classically poly-time points are the roots of unity of order n \mid 6 — the values q \in \{1, -1, \pm i, e^{\pm i\pi/3}\}.
  • Additive approximation is \mathrm{BQP}-complete at a primitive root of unity of order n \nmid 6 (Aharonov--Jones--Landau; Freedman--Kitaev--Larsen--Wang).

This stratification is cited fact, not a QOU derivation. Crucially, \#\mathrm{P}-hardness of one invariant's exact evaluation does not separate \mathrm{P} from \mathrm{NP}: it concerns counting, not decision, and no known reduction turns it into a \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} proof.

The \mathbb{G}_m-torsion stratification. Matching the citations above:

Regime Value of q Jones complexity
Classically transparent torsion, order n \mid 6 poly-time (JVW tractable set)
Quantum-hard torsion, order n \nmid 6 \mathrm{BQP}-complete additive approximation (AJL)
Counting-hard non-torsion q_0 \#\mathrm{P}-hard exact evaluation (JVW)

At a torsion root of unity of order n \mid 6 the Iwahori--Hecke algebra degenerates just enough that the invariant collapses to a poly-time formula. This — not torsion in general — is the transparent regime. At other roots of unity the algebra supports the AJL quantum algorithm (\mathrm{BQP}). At the non-torsion aether value q_0 the algebra is semisimple and exact evaluation is \#\mathrm{P}-hard.

Kummer persistence. The Kummer filtration yields \kappa_c^{\mathrm{comp}} \bmod n = 0 if and only if n \mid 6 — precisely the JVW classically-tractable set. Because q_0 is strictly non-torsion, no finite Kummer level applies: q_0 sits permanently outside the transparent set.

What is conjectural (the irreducible gap). The step from the established "\#\mathrm{P}-hard exact Jones evaluation at q_0" to the asserted "\mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP}" is an analogy, not a theorem. Two things are unproven; together they constitute the QOU faithfulness hypothesis, which is open and enters only as a hypothesis, never as an established fact:

  1. that the resolution-tree residue \mathrm{res}_{\mathcal{R}}(\chi(A)) is a faithful invariant of the \mathrm{P}-vs-\mathrm{NP} decision boundary, rather than of the (easier-to-obstruct) counting problem; and
  2. that its non-vanishing at q_0 is equivalent to \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} rather than merely implied by it.

A concrete non-vanishing of \chi(A) at generic q_0 is a Zariski-open (hence generically true, easy) condition; it therefore cannot by itself discharge the conjecture without collapsing the claimed equivalence. This genericity is itself proved: a nonzero polynomial obstruction vanishes at only finitely many parameter values, so its non-vanishing locus over an infinite domain is cofinite, hence infinite — stated over a generic integral domain, with no archimedean input. This is the chippable boundary: everything above the line is cited or provable; only the analogy remains open.

The non-vanishing leg is conditional on the Wigner axiom and the branch-point count. While the observability axiom annihilates HH^0, one-dimensionality of the degree-2 obstruction space does not follow unconditionally from untwisted Hochschild Poincaré duality HH^2 \cong (HH^1)^\vee: as recorded in the Wigner axiom, for the quantum-group Hopf algebras in play the duality that holds at q \neq 1 is Brown and Zhang's Nakayama-twisted isomorphism HH^i(H, M) \cong HH_{d-i}(H, {}_{\nu}M) into twisted Hochschild homology, whereas at the classical point q = 1 Whitehead's lemmas give H^1(\mathfrak{g}, M) = H^2(\mathfrak{g}, M) = 0. One-dimensionality \dim_k HH^2 = 1 at q \neq 1 and its archimedean evaluation onto e(TM_0) therefore enter as the explicit hypotheses (W1)--(W2) of the Wigner axiom (obstruction reduction). The remaining geometric input, the Riemann--Roch / branch-point chain that evaluates \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 (the \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 chain), reads its branch-point count off Bring's surface rather than forcing it from the categorical axioms alone. Conditional on those inputs and with q_0 strictly non-torsion, the Kummer filtration yields \mathrm{res}_{\mathcal{R}}(\chi(A)) \neq 0 at q_0 — and no step of that chain refers to computational complexity. This sharpens the collapse observation above: even conditional on the Wigner axiom, asserting the residue equivalence would derive \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} with no complexity-theoretic input, so the conjecture's complexity-theoretic burden lives entirely in items 1--2 (faithfulness of the residue for the decision boundary).

Chipping the equivalence. The conjectured equivalence decomposes into two directions, soundness \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} \Rightarrow \mathrm{res} \neq 0 and faithfulness \mathrm{res} \neq 0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP}, taken as separate hypotheses, from which the equivalence is derived. Given the derived non-vanishing, three facts are proved: soundness is automatic and carries no computational content; asserting the equivalence is exactly asserting \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP}; and the Kummer reduction of the derived value vanishes exactly at the Jaeger--Vertigan--Welsh tractable levels, -6 \bmod n = 0 \iff n \mid 6, with any real q > 1 non-torsion. The single irreducible open item is the faithfulness direction; \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} itself enters only as an opaque proposition; no complexity-theoretic model of \mathrm{P} and \mathrm{NP} is developed here.

The counting–decision gap (companion statement). Every citable hardness result at q_0 concerns counting: Jaeger--Vertigan--Welsh give \#\mathrm{P}-hardness of exact evaluation, and \mathrm{NP} \subseteq \mathrm{P}^{\#\mathrm{P}} makes \mathrm{FP} \neq \#\mathrm{P} a consequence of \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} — the weaker separation. These enter as cited hypotheses, never as established facts. Modulo those hypotheses and the residue--semisimplicity bridge, the reachable companion faithfulness is proved: if \mathrm{FP} \neq \#\mathrm{P}, a surviving residue forces exact Jones evaluation at q_0 out of \mathrm{FP}. Upgrading this to the conjectured \mathrm{res} \neq 0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} requires exactly two open inputs, carried as explicit hypotheses: the counting separation \mathrm{FP} \neq \#\mathrm{P} itself, and a counting\todecision transfer that no known result supplies. Discharging those two hypotheses is precisely what a proof of this conjecture must add. The bridge — semisimplicity of H_n(q_0) via Wenzl's root-of-unity criterion — is the one front where ordinary (non-millennium) mathematics can still advance the conjecture, and its parameter side is done: the genericity condition "q^k \neq 1 for 2 \leq k \leq n", stated over a generic monoid, is proved for every real q > 1 at every rank, and the argument composes end-to-end — for the aether q_0 > 1, given \mathrm{FP} \neq \#\mathrm{P}, exact Jones evaluation is not polynomial-time, conditional only on the two cited hypotheses. Notably the obstruction residual drops out of this reachable statement entirely: the counting hardness at q_0 rests on parameter genericity alone. Stage 2 advances this on the Schur-element side: semisimplicity is governed by non-vanishing of the Schur elements of the symmetrizing trace, and it is proved — on the concrete Schur element s_{\lambda,X}(Q) = Q^{n(\lambda)} \prod_x (1 - X Q^{c(x)})/(1 - Q^{h(x)}) — that in the regime Q > 1, X \leq 0 every Schur element is nonzero (positive hook lengths make every denominator strictly negative; nonpositive X makes every numerator positive). The Geck--Pfeiffer criterion enters as a cited hypothesis, and semisimplicity follows at every rank with the Schur leg computed rather than assumed. For physical Markov specialisations X = Q^{-N} > 0 the numerator factors genuinely vanish at cells of content N — the Temperley--Lieb quotient stratification. That is no longer a follow-on: it is proved, and the surviving blocks are characterised combinatorially — at X = Q^{-N} with N \geq 1 the Wedderburn blocks that survive are exactly the partitions with at most N columns, \lambda_1 \leq N.

It does not advance the open pair, and should not be cited as if it did. The aether provably never lands on the Temperley--Lieb locus: X \leq 0 \Rightarrow X \neq Q^{-N} is proved for every N, so the stratification describes a region of parameter space the aether avoids. The reachable counting statement consumes only semisimplicity at q_0, already discharged by Wenzl genericity from q_0 > 1; knowing which blocks die elsewhere is not one of its inputs, and fewer surviving blocks would mean a smaller algebra — the tractable direction, not the hard one. Nor is it a counting-versus-decision statement, so it cannot supply the transfer. What remains open beyond all citation is unchanged: the pair of open hypotheses of the transfer statement above.

What the QOU actually proves (the derived result, not the Clay separation). Where the conjectured \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} needs the open counting\todecision transfer, a weaker but genuinely derived statement needs none of it. The observation trace at q_0 is \#\mathrm{P}-hard (above); if extracting the degree-0 answer requires the full 3^{3n}-leaf surviving resolution tree, the Bekenstein bandwidth bound forces any bandwidth-limited device to run super-polynomially — no bandwidth-limited device decides the boundary problem in polynomial time. This physical-intractability theorem is proved, as is the exponential-domination fact it rests on. It is strictly weaker than abstract \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} — a general Turing machine is not bandwidth-limited — but it is derived, not assumed.

The fourth millennium evaluation. The QOU obstruction reduction conjectures that all classical-limit obstructions map to the scalar class \chi(A) \in HH^2 \cong k, so that \mathrm{P} vs \mathrm{NP} becomes a fourth restriction of the same class alongside RH, NS, and BSD. The proportionality of the four evaluations is part of the conjecture, not a consequence of it.

Corollary (conditional). If the obstruction-class conjecture holds, resolving \mathrm{P} vs \mathrm{NP} constrains RH, NS, and BSD and vice versa, their evaluation maps differing but the underlying class remaining identical. The corollary inherits the conjectural status of its hypothesis.
rem:skein-filtration-trichotomy:
Remark One length filtration, three problems: q-Collatz halting, P vs NP, q-NS regularity. Three hard problems reformulated inside a quantum observable universe — the q-Collatz halting question, the P versus NP boundary, and q-Navier–Stokes regularity — are the same question asked of one length filtration on the Skein aether \mathcal{S}(q) \cong \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]. Each computation is a braid word \beta \in H_n(q); its observed output is the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) (the Jones–Skein invariant an observer reads); and its complexity is graded by the crossing-number filtration \ell.

Write \ell for that filtration and \mathrm{obs} for the Markov-trace observation. The three problems differ only in what they ask of \ell along an orbit:

Reformulation Question on the filtration \ell
q-Collatz does \ell descend to the normal form (the orbit halts)?
P versus NP is the observation reachable within a polynomial \ell-budget, rather than the naive 3^{c} resolution leaves?
q-Navier–Stokes does \ell stay bounded (no finite-time blow-up of the vortex-knot complexity)?

The observation is the common, tractable shadow: because the Skein relations cut a single fixed ideal whose quotient is \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], the Markov trace is computable, so "the observed output reaches the normal form's value" follows from halting for free. The difficulty is not algebraic — it does not live in an ideal. By the Reeb-flow Turing-completeness of the aether dynamics, the halting set is undecidable, hence not cut out by any ideal; the content sits entirely in the filtration \ell.

For q-Navier–Stokes the dictionary is concrete: a vortex tube of the brane fluid is a braid word evolving in time, its closure is a knotted vortex, its conserved helicity is the Markov-trace observation, and its crossing number is \ell. A non-increasing filtration — a monotone Lyapunov complexity, the categorical form of bounded enstrophy — rules out blow-up with bound the initial complexity, the abstract shadow of the q-Beale–Kato–Majda criterion.

The legs are coupled, not merely parallel. Two consequences of the shared filtration are proved. First, a counterexample on either the descent leg or the boundedness leg destroys the shared ingredient — a controlled descent on \ell — from which the two positive conclusions are jointly derived, so the walls do not fail independently. Second, within any single system whose normal form is periodic, the boundedness question and the descent question are coupled outright: an orbit whose filtration is unbounded cannot reach the normal form, because a halting orbit lands in the attractor's cycle and thereafter visits only finitely many states, hence has bounded complexity with an explicit bound depending on that orbit. The implication runs one way only — a bounded orbit may cycle forever without ever reaching the normal form — which is why descent is the harder of the two questions.

This couples two questions asked of one instance; it does not identify a Navier--Stokes singularity with a q-Collatz divergence. The two legs are instantiated here as different systems — the q-Collatz system, whose complexity measure is a free parameter, and the vortex-reduction system, on which unbounded complexity is not even satisfiable, since that system is proved regular. Sharing the abstraction \mathtt{SkeinObservationSystem} is sharing a type, not a state.

The hypothesis the coupling needs is that the normal form be periodic, and the q-Collatz attractor satisfies it: the class \mathrm{QCollatz} carries \mathcal{C}(\mathcal{C}(\alpha)) = \alpha for the attractor \alpha, the 2-cycle \{q^{-1}, 1 + q^{-1}\} that is the q-lift of the classical \{1, 2\}. The discharge is recorded as a lemma rather than asserted, since \mathcal{C}(\mathcal{C}(\alpha)) = \alpha is periodicity at period 2 definitionally. The hypothesis is periodicity rather than the more obvious fixed-point condition \mathcal{C}(\alpha) = \alpha because that condition is not merely stronger, it is false here — the same class carries \mathcal{C}(\alpha) \neq \alpha as an axiom. A transfer stated for fixed points would be vacuous on precisely the system it was written for.

A descent measure is not a cheaper target than the conjecture. Since descent implies halting, it is tempting to read "find a descent measure for \ell" as a weaker goal than "prove q-Collatz". It is not: on a forward-invariant cone the two are equivalent, because if every element halts then the hitting time \mu(P) = \min\{k : \mathcal{C}_q^k(P) = \alpha\} is itself a strict \mathbb{N}-valued descent measure. So any search whose success criterion is the mere existence of a descent measure is searching for a restatement of the conjecture.

This sharpens rather than abandons the descent route. Its point is that an explicit, independently motivated \mu — a valuation, a degree, a contact volume — can discharge the conjecture; a candidate is worth pursuing precisely for the properties the hitting time lacks, namely computability, a closed form, and monotonicity under the algebra of [2]_q and [3]_q. The obvious candidate v_{[2]} is already refuted, scope-(a): the q-odd element P = -q^{-1} - 2 has v_{[2]}(P) = 0 while its odd branch has v_{[2]} = 2 — one candidate excluded, the class untouched.

The three legs share the aether and diverge only in the filtration question; none is settled here. Each remains an open conjecture in its own right: the q-Collatz descent measure, the faithfulness leg of the P versus NP boundary, and q-Navier–Stokes regularity are the respective open cores. What the shared structure supplies is a common language in which the tractable observation and the hard filtration question are cleanly separated.
thm:geometry-of-incompleteness:
Theorem The geometry of incompleteness: a Turing-complete QOU has a nonempty horizon. Given a QOU whose aether is Turing-complete, the jet horizon \mathcal{H} = V(\mathfrak{h}) is non-empty: there exists a degree-0 datum whose truth is inaccessible. Equivalently, the degree-0 sections vanish on a non-trivial region, \Gamma(\mathcal{H}, A_0) = 0.

A degree-0 datum is an observable answer read off the aether — a decision result, a particle identity, or the truth value of a self-referential sentence. It is inaccessible — behind the horizon — when it fails either route to access:

  • formally, it is unprovable (Gödel incompleteness, forced in any aether expressive enough to encode arithmetic — every q \neq 1 aether, whose q-Toffoli gates are universal); or
  • physically, extracting it is super-polynomial. For the boundary family a bandwidth-limited device must read the full 3^{3n}-leaf surviving skein resolution tree, so by the Bekenstein bandwidth bound its step count grows faster than every polynomial (the physical-intractability theorem).

These are two witnesses of one phenomenon — the vanishing of degree-0 sections. Gödel supplies a formally-inaccessible degree-0 datum; the resolution-tree information bound supplies a physically-intractable one. Either establishes a non-empty horizon; the QOU exhibits both, so the horizon is doubly confirmed. In the framework's reading, this common cause is exactly what a black-hole event horizon is: the region across which degree-0 truth cannot pass while degree-\geq 1 data (witnesses, Hawking radiation) leaks. The event horizon is the geometry of incompleteness.

Scope (what this does and does not say). This is an existence / necessity statement about the aether's structure — a Turing-complete QOU must host an inaccessible degree-0 region. It is not a proof of \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP}. The step from "the observation trace is intractable to extract" to "\mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP}" is a counting-to-decision transfer that no known result supplies and that a generic argument cannot (a \#\mathrm{P}-hard count can sit atop a poly-time decision, as for perfect matchings). The physical-intractability leg is genuinely derived; the formal-incompleteness leg is Gödel's theorem; only the identification of this joint inaccessibility with the black-hole horizon is the framework's degree-0 interpretation.
sec:q-heat-kernel-analysis-intro:
The aether supplies a Jackson derivative D_q and a categorical Fourier transform. One now constructs the corresponding heat kernel and extracts its spectral decomposition. This section verifies that standard heat-kernel analysis survives the q-deformation when q = q_0 is non-torsion. It also establishes a computational fallback when the Peter--Weyl sum diverges at large rank.

The construction proceeds in three steps. First, the Taylor series proposition realises the abstract grouplike \exp_q as a convergent power series. Second, the q-Gaussian proposition confirms that the q-Gaussian solves the fundamental q-heat equation \partial_t u = D_q^2 u. Third, the Peter--Weyl decomposition expands this solution in Hecke--Wedderburn characters. The closing remark provides a Perron--Frobenius truncation for large-rank evaluation. The subsequent section on Statistical Mechanics leverages this q-heat kernel as the partition function Z_q to derive quantum temperature, pressure, and volume.
prop:q-exponential-taylor:
Proposition Taylor series of \exp_q (archimedean). Let R be a commutative ring of characteristic zero in which all Jackson factorials [n]_q! = \prod_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1 - q^k}{1 - q} are invertible. Over R, the convergent power series

  \exp_q(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} \frac{x^n}{[n]_q!}

represents the abstract grouplike \exp_q \in G(\mathcal{H}_q).

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs—real-valued physical observables, bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at q_0. Categorical identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is strictly specialised here.
prf:q-exponential-taylor:
Proof Proof of q exponential taylor. The categorical defining equation D_q\, \exp_q = \exp_q, joined with the boundary condition \exp_q(0) = 1, determines a unique formal power series \exp_q(x) = \sum_{n\ge 0} a_n x^n in R[\![x]\!]. The Jackson derivative acts on monomials via D_q(x^n) = [n]_q\, x^{n-1}. One substitutes this into the equation:

  D_q\,\sum_n a_n x^n
  \;=\; \sum_{n \ge 0} a_n [n]_q x^{n-1}
  \;=\; \sum_{m \ge 0} a_{m+1} [m+1]_q x^m.

Equating this to \sum_m a_m x^m forces the recursion a_{m+1} = a_m / [m+1]_q. With a_0 = 1, one obtains:

  a_n \;=\; \prod_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{[k]_q} \;=\; \frac{1}{[n]_q!}.

This verifies the claimed coefficient. Convergence on a neighbourhood of 0 holds because [n]_q! \to \infty faster than geometrically when |q| < 1 or |q| > 1. When |q| = 1, write q = e^{2\pi i\theta}; for irrational \theta convergence holds by Diophantine estimates on \theta. This series provides the archimedean realisation of the universal grouplike. Its existence over \mathbb{C} forms a theorem about the \mathbb{C}-fibre of the moduli of grouplikes over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}], not a redefinition of \exp_q. \qed

Special values.

Regime [n]_q! asymptotic \exp_q(x) behaviour
q = 1 n! (classical) \exp_q(x) = e^x (ordinary exponential)
0 < q < 1 (1 - q)^{-n}\,n!\,(1 + O(q^n)) slow-growth; radius \infty
q > 1 q^{\binom{n}{2}}\,n!_{q^{-1}} faster-than-classical growth
q \to \infty q^{\binom{n}{2}} entire, type \log q

Relation to physical constants. Evaluating at the QOU aether value q_0 (local aether q) yields e_{q_0}(x) = \sum x^n / [n]_{q_0}!. This series generates the moments of the Reeb-flow distribution on \mathcal{S}. Because [n]_{q_0}! \sim q_0^{\binom{n}{2}} n!_{q_0^{-1}} grows super-exponentially at q_0 \approx 1.11, the series converges for all x \in \mathbb{C}.
prop:q-gaussian-solves-q-heat:
Proposition Reeb-invariant q-Gaussian solves the q-heat equation (archimedean). Over \mathbb{R}^n with the archimedean realisation of the q-Laplacian, the Reeb-invariant q-Gaussian

  G_q(t, x) = \bigl(4\pi q^{-2} t\bigr)^{-n/2} \exp\!\left(-\frac{q^2  |x|^2}{4t}\right)

is a fundamental solution of the q-heat equation:

  \partial_t G_q = -\Delta_q G_q, \qquad \lim_{t \downarrow 0} G_q(t, \cdot) = \delta_0.
prf:q-gaussian-solves-q-heat:
Proof Proof of q gaussian solves q heat. One decomposes \Delta_q into its three components:

  \Delta_q \;=\; q^{-2} \Delta
  + q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})\,\mathfrak{C}
  + (1 - q^{-1})^2\,\Delta_\xi.

The operator \mathfrak{C} is the Coriolis cross-coupling and \Delta_\xi is the pure Reeb-spin Laplacian. Both \mathfrak{C} and \Delta_\xi contain at least one factor of \mathcal{L}_\xi or \iota_\xi.

The Gaussian G_q depends only on the base coordinates x \in M, not on the Reeb-fibre direction. Therefore,

  \mathcal{L}_\xi G_q = 0,
  \qquad
  \iota_\xi G_q = 0.

Both the Coriolis and spin contributions vanish on G_q:

  -\Delta_q G_q \;=\; -q^{-2} \Delta G_q \;=\; q^{-2} \nabla^2 G_q.

Here \nabla^2 = \sum \partial_i^2 is the non-positive analyst's Laplacian and \Delta = -\nabla^2 is the non-negative Hodge Laplacian. Direct differentiation yields

  \partial_t G_q \;=\; G_q \left(
    -\frac{n}{2t} + \frac{q^2 |x|^2}{4t^2}
  \right),
  \quad
  \nabla^2 G_q \;=\; G_q \left(
    -\frac{n q^2}{2 t} + \frac{q^4 |x|^2}{4 t^2}
  \right).

Multiplying the second equation by q^{-2} yields the first. Hence \partial_t G_q = -\Delta_q G_q. The initial-data condition G_q(t,\cdot) \to \delta_0 as t \downarrow 0 follows from standard properties of the Gaussian heat kernel. \square

Existence at arbitrary q > 0. The formula for G_q defines a classical Gaussian with variance \sigma^2 = t/q^2. It is convergent and strictly positive for every q > 0 and t > 0. At the physical aether value q_0 \approx 1.11 (local aether q), the q-Gaussian

  G_{q_0}(t, x) \;=\; \bigl(4\pi t / q_0^2\bigr)^{-n/2}
  \exp\!\left(-\frac{q_0^2  |x|^2}{4t}\right)

is a strict density with variance \sigma^2 \approx 0.81\,t. This is narrower than the classical Gaussian by a factor of q_0^{-2} \approx 0.81. No convergence obstruction appears in the archimedean realisation of the q-heat kernel at q_0 > 1.
rem:q-gaussian-solves-q-heat-interpretat:
Remark Time-rescaling interpretation of the Reeb-invariant q-Gaussian. Because -\Delta_q = q^{-2}\nabla^2 on Reeb-invariant forms, defining \tau = q^{-2} t yields

  G_q(t, x) = \bigl(4\pi \tau\bigr)^{-n/2} \exp\!\bigl(-|x|^2 / (4 \tau)\bigr).

This matches the classical Gaussian heat kernel in rescaled time. Reeb-invariant diffusion on a QOU with aether parameter q is isomorphic to ordinary diffusion with the clock running at rate q^{-2}.

At the Big Bang (q \to \infty), the clock freezes. Heat cannot spread on the base because the Reeb-fibre direction completely absorbs the diffusive budget. At heat death (q \to 1), the clock runs at unit rate, and G_q exactly recovers the classical Gaussian.
prop:q-heat-kernel-peter-weyl:
Proposition Peter--Weyl decomposition of the q-heat kernel (archimedean). Applying the categorical Fourier transform to the q-heat equation diagonalises the q-Laplacian on each Peter--Weyl isotypic component of \mathbf{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)), yielding an explicit spectral formula for the q-heat kernel in two parts.

  1. Spectral decomposition. A solution u \colon \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \times \mathcal{S} \to \mathbb{C} to \partial_t u = -\Delta_q u with initial datum u_0 decomposes as
  u(t, x) = \sum_{\lambda \in \widehat{H_n(q)}} d_\lambda(q) \cdot e^{-\mu_\lambda(q)\,t} \cdot \pi_\lambda(u_0)(x).

The sum ranges over irreducible Wedderburn blocks of the Hecke algebra H_n(q), equivalently indexed by partitions \lambda \vdash n. The dimension d_\lambda(q) is the Steinberg q-hook dimension, \pi_\lambda projects onto the V_\lambda-isotypic component, and \mu_\lambda(q) denotes the q-Laplacian eigenvalue.

  1. Explicit content-Casimir formula. Given a partition \lambda \vdash n with cell contents c(\square) = j - i, the Reeb-spin eigenvalue on V_\lambda is
  \mu_\lambda(q) = \sum_{\square \in \lambda}  [c(\square)]_q \, [c(\square) + 1]_q,

where [k]_q = (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1}) is the symmetric quantum integer. It is the eigenvalue on V_\lambda of the Reeb-holonomy Laplacian

  \Delta_\xi^{(q)} = (q - q^{-1})^{-2} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \bigl( q\,H_k + q^{-1} H_k^{-1} - (q + q^{-1}) \bigr), \qquad H_k = (\Delta^2_{k-1})^{-1}\Delta^2_k,

where \Delta^2_k is the full twist of the first k+1 strands. Each H_k is the k-th Jucys--Murphy element of H_n(q), and \Delta_\xi^{(q)} is central. Writing q = e^{h}, each summand is a symmetric second difference of step h, and as h \to 0 the operator tends to \sum_k X_k(X_k+1), where X_k are the classical Jucys--Murphy elements. So \Delta_\xi^{(q)} is the finite-step form of the Reeb Laplacian \mathcal{L}_\xi^*\mathcal{L}_\xi, with a half-integer shift. The Reeb part of \Delta_q enters with weight 1, not \hbar_q^2: on a mode with no horizontal derivative, d_q and \delta_q reduce to d and \delta, because q^{-1} + \hbar_q = 1. The classical-core and cross-coupling terms of rem:q-laplacian-expansion act on such modes as well, and the three coefficients sum to (q^{-1} + \hbar_q)^2 = 1. The spatial part contributes a separate eigenvalue q^{-2}|\mathbf{k}|^2, dependent on the spatial wavenumber \mathbf{k}.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Any categorical identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
prf:q-heat-kernel-peter-weyl:
Proof Proof of q heat kernel peter weyl.

Scope note. The eigenvalue formula uses symmetric q-integers and unit Reeb weight (no \hbar_q^2 prefactor); both choices are derived below rather than fitted. What is proved: the operator is central. Its Jucys--Murphy elements are relative full twists. Its eigenvalue on a Jucys--Murphy weight vector is (q-q^{-1})^2\sum[c][c+1]. The weight vectors exist for generic q by the seminormal form. What is not proved: that \Delta^2_k is the holonomy of the Reeb rotation loop of the cluster of the first k+1 points. That identification is Bridge A (the n-body base with \xi the Euler field, plus Drinfeld--Kohno). The weight-1 argument for the Reeb part is written out below; unlike the statements listed as proved, it has not been independently checked. The binding computation already uses this \mu_\lambda, so no number moves. The deuteron term of the unified iterative correction at the proton q_0 is still -17.69 MeV against AME +2.2246 MeV, the wrong sign. That problem is downstream of \mu_\lambda and is not addressed here.

Proof. Schur's lemma on the irreducible Wedderburn block forces any central element to act by a scalar. For \Delta_\xi^{(q)} that scalar is computed on a Jucys--Murphy weight vector. There H_k = L_k acts by q^{2c_k}, and each summand becomes (q^{c} - q^{-c})(q^{c+1} - q^{-c-1}) = (q - q^{-1})^2[c][c+1]. Summing over k gives \mu_\lambda(q). The value [c][c+1] is unchanged under c \mapsto -c-1, so each cell contributes the U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) Casimir value at spin c or -c-1, whichever is non-negative.

The Reeb part carries no \hbar_q^2. Let f be a mode with df = (\xi f)\,\varTheta. Then d_q f = q^{-1}(\xi f)\varTheta + \hbar_q(\xi f)\varTheta = df. For a 1-form g\varTheta, adjointness alone gives \delta(g\varTheta) = \mathcal{L}_\xi^* g, and \iota_\xi(g\varTheta) = g, so \delta_q(g\varTheta) = (q^{-1} + \hbar_q)\mathcal{L}_\xi^* g = \delta(g\varTheta). Hence \Delta_q f = \mathcal{L}_\xi^*\mathcal{L}_\xi f with weight 1. On Hecke blocks the Reeb Laplacian is realised by its finite-step form \Delta_\xi^{(q)}. \square

Remark Convergence, the q-Gaussian equilibrium mode, and the place in the q-heat story. Small-\lambda table (at physical aether q_0 \approx 1.11, symmetric quantum integers, values computed at the corpus anchor q_0 = 1.1099786\ldots):

See Table.

The content-Casimir sum follows explicitly from partition data. No diagonalisation is required to determine the spectrum.

Convergence and Mercer. For t > 0, the sum converges absolutely. Every eigenvalue satisfies \mu_\lambda(q) \ge \sum_{\square} c(\square)(c(\square)+1) \ge 0 for real q > 0, because each cell contributes [j]_q[j+1]_q with j \ge 0 and [m]_q \ge m there. That the eigenvalues grow fast enough in n for e^{-\mu_\lambda(q)\, t} to beat the dimension weights is the convergence conjecture of the q-heat kernel; it is not proved. The dimension weights d_\lambda(q) grow at most polynomially. The sum is Mercer-type, defining a continuous kernel K_q(t; x, y) on \mathcal{S} \times \mathcal{S} for every t > 0.

Relation to the Reeb-invariant q-Gaussian. The trivial partition \lambda = (1) carries \mu_{(1)}(q) = 0. Its Peter--Weyl component remains constant in t, representing the equilibrium distribution as t \to \infty. The partitions \lambda = (2) and (1,1) contribute the leading Reeb-invariant heat flow, recovering the q-Gaussian. Higher-order partitions produce Reeb-fibre modulations wholly absent from the base-Gaussian.

Role in the q-heat story. This constitutes the Fourier-side of the heat flow. Every solution decomposes into exponentially decaying H_n(q)-isotypic modes with closed-form decay rates \mu_\lambda(q). The Laplace transform \mathcal{L}[u](s) = \sum_\lambda d_\lambda(q) (\mu_\lambda(q) + s)^{-1} \pi_\lambda(u_0) acts as the resolvent of \Delta_q, with simple poles precisely at s = -\mu_\lambda(q). The q-dilogarithm generates \sum_\lambda \log \mu_\lambda(q). This serves as the partition function of the Reeb-heat flow.
rem:q-heat-kernel-computational-fallback:
Remark Computational fallback at large k: q-heat kernel and Perron--Frobenius. At the physical aether value q_0 \approx 1.11, exact enumeration of H_n(q) irreducibles \lambda \vdash n becomes infeasible for large n. The partition count grows as p(n) \sim \exp(\pi\sqrt{2n/3})/(4n\sqrt{3}), hitting \sim 10^6 at n = 50. Exact character-table computations fail beyond an exactness threshold k_{\mathrm{exact}} \approx 9--15.

Fallback via the q-heat kernel. For k > k_{\mathrm{exact}}, the Peter--Weyl decomposition supplies a principled approximation:

  \mathrm{tr}\,M_\lambda(W_N) \approx d_\lambda(q_0) \cdot e^{-\mu_\lambda(q_0)  s_* N}.

Here s_* = \hbar_{q_0} = (q_0 - 1)/q_0 \approx 0.0988 is the canonical Reeb-time scale, and \mu_\lambda(q_0) is the content-Casimir eigenvalue.

Equivalence to Perron--Frobenius. This strictly corresponds to the Perron--Frobenius dominant-eigenvalue approximation:

  \ln\bigl|\mathrm{Tr}\,M_\lambda(\text{step})\bigr| \approx \ln d_q(\lambda) + N(\text{step}) \cdot \ln|\mu_\lambda|.

The dominant \mu_\lambda for the mean inter-nucleon crossing is the q-Casimir eigenvalue of the symmetric representation \lambda = (2):

  \mu_{(2)}(q_0) = \hbar_{q_0}^2  [1]_{q_0}[2]_{q_0} \approx 0.021.

The approximation \ln q_0 \approx 0.104 agrees with s_* = \hbar_{q_0} \approx 0.099 to leading order in \hbar_q.

Gaussian approximation at very large N. At extremely large N, a Gaussian profile dominates the Peter--Weyl sum. The Plancherel central-limit theorem for the random walk on Young diagrams yields:

  \mathrm{tr}\,M_\lambda(W_N) \approx d_\lambda(q_0) \cdot G_{q_0}(N, \lambda_{\mathrm{centroid}}).

The kernel G_q is the Reeb-invariant q-Gaussian. Because G_q is a classical Gaussian with rescaled variance \sigma^2 = t/q^2, it remains well-defined at q_0 > 1. The distribution simply narrows by a factor of 0.81 relative to the classical case. No convergence obstruction manifests.

Computational protocol. The numerical workflow proceeds in three stages:

  1. Small k \le k_{\mathrm{exact}}: Enumerate all \lambda \vdash k and compute \mathrm{tr}\,M_\lambda exactly via Hecke character tables.
  2. Moderate k_{\mathrm{exact}} < k \le k_{\mathrm{PF}}: Deploy the Perron--Frobenius shortcut utilizing the content-Casimir formula for \mu_\lambda.
  3. Large k > k_{\mathrm{PF}}: Invoke the Plancherel-Gaussian approximation. Sum over dominant partitions inside a variance-\sigma^2 neighbourhood of \lambda_{\mathrm{centroid}}.

Each stage truncates the Peter--Weyl sum systematically. Stage 2 isolates the dominant exponential mode. Stage 3 isolates the leading Gaussian envelope.

Relation to previous methods. The Perron--Frobenius truncation exactly duplicates the stage-2 approximation. The previously discarded Bożejko--Speicher q-Gaussian restricted to |q| \le 1. The QOU q-heat-kernel Gaussian subsumes it, remaining valid at q_0 > 1 while reflecting the Peter--Weyl decomposition of the Reeb flow.
sec:stat-mech-intro:
The statistical mechanical structure of the QOU acts not as an analogy, but as the exact mechanism by which continuous physics emerges from discrete Reeb dynamics. The Planck time t_P(q) = q/(q-1) functions strictly as the inverse temperature \beta. It counts the number of microscopic operations (Julia set iterations on the exceptional divisor) comprising each macroscopic time unit.

The thermodynamic limit \beta \to \infty (q \to 1) coincides with the classical limit. Infinitely many discrete operations average into smooth Reeb flow, precisely as infinitely many molecular collisions average into thermodynamic equilibrium. The subsequent continuous-approximation corrections are O(1/\beta) = O(\hbar_q). Consequently, quantum-gravitational effects are finite-size corrections to the thermodynamic limit of time.

This section derives the partition function, entropy, and free energy of the Reeb dynamics. These quantities establish the statistical mechanical framework underlying information-theoretic time.
def:quantum-entropy:
Definition Quantum entropy as a non-abelian surface integral. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with aether parameter q, and let U \subset M be a region. The quantum entropy of U is the non-abelian surface integral

  S_q(U) = -\,\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{Ad}} \!\oint_{\partial U} \omega_{\mathcal{F}} \,\wedge\, *\eta_q,

where \mathcal{F} = \mathrm{Ad}(A) is the adjoint bundle, \omega_{\mathcal{F}} is the adjoint connection, \eta_q = (2q-1)/q^3 is the operational entropy density, and * is the Hodge star on \partial U.
rem:quantum-entropy-remark: Remark Surface independence of the quantum entropy. The measurability conditions c_1(\mathcal{F}) = 0 and c_2(\mathcal{F}) = 0 ensure that the surface integral defining S_q(U) is independent of the choice of bounding surface, via the Yekutieli non-abelian Stokes theorem.
def:quantum-temperature:
Definition Quantum temperature. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with aether parameter q and Planck time t_P(q) = q/(q-1) = 1/\hbar_q. The quantum temperature of a region U \subset M is

  T_q(U) = \hbar_q = \frac{q - 1}{q},

and the inverse temperature is \beta_q = 1/T_q = t_P(q).
rem:quantum-temperature-remark:
Remark Temperature, aether density and entropy. The Kashaev volume--density reading introduces the aether density \rho_q = 1/\hbar_q^{2}. In these terms, the temperature and its inverse square are

  T_q = \rho_q^{-1/2}, \qquad \beta_q^{2} = \rho_q.

Temperature and aether density form conjugate square roots. A state at high drag density (small \hbar_q) rests at low temperature, while the inverse-temperature squared matches the density itself. This relationship absorbs several dimensional-analysis identities.

The quantum temperature remains the thermodynamic conjugate of the quantum entropy S_q(U):

  \frac{1}{T_q} = \frac{\partial S_q}{\partial \mathfrak{E}_q}\bigg|_V = \frac{1}{\hbar_q}.
rem:quantum-temperature-interpretation:
Remark Temperature as tick rate and surface quantity. Classical statistical mechanics defines temperature implicitly through the Boltzmann distribution \rho \propto e^{-\beta H}, where \beta = 1/(k_B T) enforces energy conservation. In the QOU, \beta_q holds direct operational meaning: it counts the discrete Reeb operations composing one macroscopic time unit. Temperature is the tick rate of the quantum aether, not a statistical average over kinetic energies.

Surface character of temperature. The entropy S_q(U) integrates strictly over the surface \partial U, guided by two principles.

First, the non-abelian Stokes theorem converts the bulk curvature integral to a boundary holonomy. The flatness conditions render this integral independent of the bounding surface choice. Entropy constitutes pure boundary datum.

Second, the Frobenius pairing is non-degenerate, so the categorical trace detects every nonzero endomorphism of U. Non-degeneracy alone does not bound the number of distinguishable states in U by data on \partial U; no such bound is proved here, and the reading of \partial U as controlling the state count is a heuristic, not a holographic theorem. Temperature, as the energy derivative of entropy, inherits whatever boundary character the entropy has from the first principle.

Classical limit. As q \to 1, T_q \to 0 and \beta_q \to \infty, sending S_q(U) \to S_{\mathrm{classical}}(U). The non-abelian Stokes integral degenerates to the classical Gauss law. The Frobenius trace becomes the ordinary matrix trace. The Boltzmann constant emerges as k_B = \hbar_q / T_{\mathrm{phys}} in the correspondence limit, where physical temperature T_{\mathrm{phys}} is measured in SI units.
def:quantum-pressure:
Definition Quantum pressure. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with quantum temperature T_q = \hbar_q, let U \subset M be a region of the brane with boundary \partial U and quantum volume V_q, and let \mathfrak{S}_q(K) be the categorical action of a knot configuration K in U. The quantum pressure on \partial U is

  P_q(U) = -\,\frac{\partial F_q}{\partial V_q}\bigg|_{T_q},

where F_q = -T_q \ln Z_q is the quantum free energy and

  Z_q(U) = \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{Ad}} \!\sum_{K \,\in\, \mathrm{Conf}(U)} e^{-\beta_q \, \mathfrak{S}_q(K)}

is the partition function over the configuration space \mathrm{Conf}(U) of knot states in U, with \beta_q = 1/\hbar_q = t_P(q).
rem:quantum-pressure-remark:
Remark Bulk and boundary pressure. The quantum pressure decomposes into bulk and boundary components:

  P_q = P_q^{(\mathrm{bulk})} + P_q^{(\mathrm{boundary})}.

The bulk term represents the volume derivative of \ln Z_q at fixed boundary conditions. The boundary term arises directly from the q-anomaly (d_q^2 \neq 0) at \partial U:

  P_q^{(\mathrm{boundary})} = \frac{\hbar_q^2}{V_q} \,\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{Ad}} \!\oint_{\partial U} \langle d_q K \,,\, d_q K \rangle_A,

where \langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle_A is the Frobenius pairing.

Archimedean specialisation. The pressure sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall and invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Any categorical identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
rem:quantum-pressure-interpretation:
Remark Pressure from Frobenius pairing, not billiard balls. Classical kinetic pressure arises from billiard-ball momentum transfer at a boundary. This classical derivation assumes point particles, elastic reflection, and a passive wall. All three assumptions fail in the QOU.

First, particles are knots, not points. The configuration K forms a braid closure strictly within the Reeb bundle S^3 \to \mathcal{S}_p.

Second, the boundary formally participates in the Hecke algebra. Momentum transfer at \partial U operates via the Frobenius pairing. A morphism K approaching \partial U pairs directly with the boundary datum via \langle K|_{\partial U}\,,\, \partial U \rangle_A, yielding a scalar in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}).

Third, the q-anomaly from d_q^2 \neq 0 renders the momentum transfer structurally inelastic. Each interaction with the boundary shifts the action by \delta \mathfrak{S}_q \propto \hbar_q^2. This shift contributes a direct, finite-size quantum correction to the pressure.

Consequently, the boundary pressure P_q^{(\mathrm{boundary})} has no classical analogue. It vanishes identically as q \to 1 (where \hbar_q \to 0) and drives the quantum corrections to the ideal gas law.

Operationally, quantum pressure measures the rate at which the partition function scales under dilation of U. Expanding U by \delta V_q admits new knot configurations into \mathrm{Conf}(U). As the Reeb bundle gains volume, geometrically longer braids become available. The pressure quantifies the structural information cost, measured in units of T_q, per unit volume of these newly available configurations.
def:quantum-volume:
Definition Quantum volume. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe, and let \mathcal{S} \to M be the state bundle with Reeb bundle S^3 \to \mathcal{S}_p at each brane point p. The quantum volume of a region U \subset M is

  V_q(U) = \int_U \mathrm{Vol}_{S^3}(\mathcal{S}_p)\; \epsilon_q(p),

where \epsilon_q is the categorical volume form on \Lambda^2 V.
rem:quantum-volume-remark:
Remark Quantum volume of a homogeneous gas. The categorical volume form \epsilon_q is uniquely preserved by the rigid duality of (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau).

For a homogeneous gas exhibiting uniform q throughout U, all fibres are strictly isometric. This yields

  V_q(U) = |U| \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(S^3_q),

where |U| is the number of brane points in U. The term

  \mathrm{Vol}(S^3_q) = \pi^2 \cdot [2]_q = \pi^2(q + q^{-1})

is the explicitly evaluated volume of S^3 measured in the q-deformed metric. At q = 1, this recovers the classical volume \mathrm{Vol}(S^3) = 2\pi^2.
rem:quantum-volume-interpretation:
Remark Volume as knot capacity of S^3 fibres. The quantum volume determines the complete configuration space \mathrm{Conf}(U) available to particle knots. A knot K bearing n crossings demands a minimal S^3 volume, strictly proportional to n \cdot \hbar_q, to embed within a fibre. The total number of single-fibre configurations at a brane point p scales as

  |\mathrm{Conf}_p| \sim \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(S^3_q)}{n_K \cdot \hbar_q},

where n_K is the crossing number of K. For a gas of N hydrogen atoms, each uniquely modeled by the knot structure \mathcal{A}(1,0), the total configuration count scales exponentially as |\mathrm{Conf}(U)| \sim |\mathrm{Conf}_p|^{|U|}.

The q-deformation stretches or compresses the Hopf fibres of the S^1 \hookrightarrow S^3 \to S^2 fibration according to the aether parameter.

Classical limit. As q \to 1, the integer analogue [2]_q \to 2. The fibre volume smoothly approaches 2\pi^2. The quantum volume V_q(U) reduces to the standard Riemannian volume of U scaled by the classic S^3 volume. The categorical volume form \epsilon_q degenerates identically to the standard Riemannian volume element.
